name: FCA Enhanced KYC Requirements Guidance - March 2026
description: FCA issued enhanced guidance on Know Your Customer procedures for high-risk customers, effective March 1, 2026. The guidance introduces new requirements for beneficial ownership verification (>25% ownership threshold), source of funds documentation for deposits exceeding £10,000, and enhanced quarterly monitoring for high-risk customer categories including PEPs, foreign nationals, and high-value customers.
context: FCA has issued enhanced guidance on Know Your Customer (KYC) procedures for high-risk customers.
All staff must be aware of new requirements before March 1, 2026.
Beneficial Ownership: If customer is a company/trust, we must verify actual owners (>25% ownership)
Source of Funds: Large deposits (>£10,000) require explanation of where money came from
Enhanced Monitoring: High-risk customers (PEP, foreign, high-value) reviewed quarterly not annually

name: Beneficial Ownership Verification
description: Compliance obligation to verify actual beneficial owners of corporate and trust customers with ownership stakes exceeding 25%. Staff must request and verify shareholders lists and director information when opening accounts for company customers.
context: If customer is a company/trust, we must verify actual owners (>25% ownership)
Customer is limited company. Ask: 'Who are the beneficial owners of this company?'
Verify: Request shareholders list, director information

name: Source of Funds Documentation
description: Compliance requirement to collect and verify source of funds documentation for customer deposits exceeding £10,000. Staff must request supporting evidence such as payslips, savings statements, or business accounts to explain the origin of large deposits.
context: Large deposits (>£10,000) require explanation of where money came from
If opening account, collect source of funds info for large deposits
Ask: 'Where is this deposit coming from?' (salary, savings, business, inheritance?)
Verify: Request recent payslip, savings statement, or business accounts

name: High-Risk Customer Periodic Refresh
description: Enhanced monitoring requirement for high-risk customer categories including PEPs, foreign nationals, and high-value customers. These customers must be reviewed and re-verified on a quarterly basis rather than the standard annual cycle.

name: ICO Subject Access Request Handling Procedures Update
description: ICO clarification on Subject Access Request (SAR) handling procedures requiring response within 30 days instead of 60, with restrictions on extensions and mandatory electronic format delivery. No fees permitted unless request is clearly unfounded.
context: ICO (UK data protection regulator) clarified Subject Access Request (SAR) handling procedures. We must respond to SARs within 30 days, not 60.
Response Deadline: 30 days (not 60) from request date
Extensions: Only if request is complex; must explain why to customer
Format: Must provide data in electronic format (CSV, PDF, etc.)

name: Subject Access Request Handling Process

name: Phishing Alert – Real Attempt in Branch
description: A confirmed social engineering attack attempt on 2026-02-08 at London Canary Wharf branch, where a fraudster posed as bank security staff to gain customer account access. Staff correctly declined the request. The alert documents red flags, response procedures, and escalation contacts for all staff to prevent similar incidents.
context: On February 8, 2026, a customer arrived at London Canary Wharf branch claiming to be 'security team' requesting customer account access to 'verify fraud.' Suspected social engineering attack. Staff correctly declined.
Alert: Fraudsters may approach branches pretending to be bank staff.
Visitor claims to be from bank wanting account access
Report suspicious activity immediately to manager

name: Security Team
description: The security function responsible for receiving and investigating fraud alerts and suspicious activity reports from branch staff and customers. Operates an alert email and emergency hotline for urgent security incidents.
context: Report To: Security Alert email: security@firstuk.bank
If urgent: Manager immediately + 0800-555-SECURITY

name: Branch Staff
description: All bank employees, particularly those in branch locations, who are the target audience for this phishing alert. Staff are responsible for verifying visitor and caller identity, protecting customer data and credentials, and reporting suspicious activity.
context: Audience: All Staff
Staff correctly declined.
Never share customer data without proper authorization
Never share staff login credentials

name: Verify Caller Identity Using Known Number
description: A mandatory procedure for all staff to verify the identity of callers or visitors claiming to be from the bank by calling back using a known, independently verified number rather than any number provided by the caller.

name: Report Suspicious Activity to Manager
